title: Ripple memory
description: A silver-green water surface remembers each disturbance as overlapping waves.
useCase: Add persistent, propagating ripple interaction to a procedural reflective surface.
interaction: Drag or press Enter on the water; adjust depth.
reducedMotion: The simulation clock stops. Deliberate pointer or keyboard disturbances update a static surface.
limitations: Requires WebGL 1; a static CSS swatch appears if unavailable or after context loss. A bounded 128×128 CPU height solver displayed with WebGL reflection; no arbitrary DOM refraction or GPU compute dependency.
look: Muted slate-teal liquid surface with glossy silver-green highlights and warped reflected vertical bands, distorted by overlapping ripple rings.
motion: Pointer presses, drags and Enter add disturbances to a 128×128 CPU wave-equation height field whose ripples spread and slowly damp; an automatic drop lands every 2.4 s.
adapt: Ripples come from `disturb` (Gaussian falloff 1200, amplitude 0.27) and `evolve`, a damped wave step (0.44 Laplacian, 0.996 decay) on the 128×128 `heights` grid uploaded as a texture; `FRAGMENT` shades it, `u_control` setting depth. Tune the 2.4 s auto-drop in `advance`.
